The Department of Public Works (DPW) provides free graffiti removal services using "blast" trucks for mineral surfaces and paint trucks for surfaces like metal or wood. They also strive to promptly remove any new graffiti if a cleaned building is tagged again. Residents can report graffiti by submitting a "Graffiti Removal Request".


If you provide an email or cell phone number you will be provided with a tracking number that will allow you to check the status of your service request and receive updates if available. Be sure to include the exact location of the graffiti, whether it's on public or private property, and the surface type that needs cleaning.


The City relies on community groups, block clubs, chambers of commerce, and individual residents to report graffiti and request removal. DPW collaborates with the Police Department to apprehend graffiti vandals and holds parents or guardians liable for damages caused by minors in their household. By reporting graffiti and taking preventative measures, such as painting over graffiti-prone locations, installing motion-sensor lighting, and planting thorny shrubs, we can work together to make our city an even more beautiful city

If you're a resident of the City and your garbage wasn't collected, you can report a Missed Pick-Up Request.


Be sure to indicate whether only your garbage pickup was missed or if the entire alley was missed. When you provide your email or cell phone number, you'll receive a tracking number that will allow you to check the status of your service request and receive updates if available.


If you're unsure of your garbage and/or recycling pickup schedules, you can call 311.

What is a pothole?
Potholes are typically irregularly shaped pavement holes which are formed when cracks in roadway pavement surfaces allow water to seep under the pavement during winter freeze and thaw weather cycles. As subsurface water freezes, it causes an expansion in the surface crack, creating what we see as potholes. Potholes are normally irregular in shape and size and tend to be relatively shallow holes, with the base of the roadway still observable.

What is a cave-in?
Cave-ins can occur when underground utility services are damaged. They are usually found near a manhole or catch basin. Cave-ins, sometimes called sinkholes, can range from a slight dip in the pavement surface to a deep hole that requires immediate attention. If the hole appears to be a potential pavement cave-in you can submit a request for a Pavement Cave-In Inspection via 311.

Who fixes potholes and cave-ins?
When a cave-in or sinkhole is reported, Transportation inspectors will assess the degree of damage and determine what caused the problem. It will then forward its assessment to the agency or utility company that needs to make the repairs. Depending on what caused the cave-in, underground work may need to be completed before pavement repairs are made.
 
Department of Transportation has inspectors in neighborhoods across the city and construction crews assigned to repair potholes throughout the year. The months of December through April is when the city typically sees the highest number of potholes, Department of Transportation schedules crews to work every day, including weekends during ‘pothole season’. However, crews work throughout the spring, summer, and fall as well.

Department of Transportation uses several techniques that enable the department to fill hundreds of thousands of potholes each year.
• Computerized mapping and tracking of potholes reported to the City’s 311 system
• Seven-day-a-week deployment of pothole repair crews during the winter months, including weekend crews and an overnight crew
• The use of high-performance cold-patch asphalt material for pothole repairs during the winter months and hot mix asphalt in spring, summer, and fall.

"Street Light Out Complaints" are tracked by the Department of Transportation to discover and monitor outage trends.


If you provide an email or cell phone number you will be provided with a tracking number that will allow you to check the status of your service request and receive updates if available.


If you are experiencing entire blocks of street lights that are consistently having issues, you may contact your local Councilor’s office for other City sponsored capital improvement programs.

City residents can submit a "Tree Pruning/Maintenance” request for Parks Department to trim trees, pick up branches or other larger landscaping waste (on Public property only).


When you provide an email or cell phone number, you'll receive a tracking number that enables you to check the status of your service request and receive updates if available. Additional information regarding the approximate size of the tree/debris and its location will be required.


Response times may vary as the Park Department’s specialized equipment is also used to address tree emergencies, often caused by storms and resulting in debris blocking the public way.

 

Note for Tree Emergency Issues

If you encounter a tree emergency, such as a fallen or hanging tree limb that is blocking the public way or obstructing traffic control measures please call 311 immediately. Note: this Service Request type is not available via the 311 app, or the 311 web portal.


If you provide an email or cell phone number you will be provided with a tracking number that will allow you to check the status of your service request and receive updates if available.


The Parks Department will quickly dispatch an inspector and/or tree trimming crew. The City’s response times can vary based on the severity of the emergency and weather conditions. The City works hard to maintain the tree population and respond to all tree-related issues as quickly and efficiently as possible.


For more information or questions please call 311.
